First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {b}^{\,px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p\operatorname{ln}⁡(b)}{b}^{\,px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{5}^{x/2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}{5}^{x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{2\cdot {5}^{x/2}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}]}_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{5}^{x/2}]}_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(1-{5}^{a/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a/2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={5}^{x/2}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{5}^{x/2}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{5}^{x/2}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14056962/assets/141d1745dc939ca63155ca3313257f385af6d3c505c16bd63ba3b91e1e0ba64b.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{5}^{x/2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (1-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$
